clue.text: NATO not having to conceal incendiary weapon

indicators.note: not having tells us the word to is dropped from the letters of NATO

parts.note: taken as written
to palm a card is to conceal it in the hand

explanation.surface: A complaint that the alliance refuses to hide a firebomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' removes TO from NATO, leaving NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Jellied petrol used in firebombs, a classic incendiary munition.

clue.text: Where one might have room to swing weapon used in the dark?

definitions.text: Where one might have room to swing
definitions.meaning: a venue for dancing late in the evening, where one swings to music
a cudgel for after dark, playing on a baton carried at nights

explanation.walkthrough: 'Swing' suggests swinging a cat or a club, but it is dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue for late-night dancing, and humorously a cosh for after dark.

clue.text: One in small platoon forbidding traveller wanting to visit shrine

indicators.note: in means the one letter goes inside the platoon abbreviation

parts.note: PL is the short form of platoon
I is the Roman numeral for one
grim means stern or forbidding

explanation.surface: A soldier in a stern little unit longs to visit a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone making a journey to a sacred place.

clue.text: Deadly obstruction — not all stop

parts.note: in tennis a let is a hindrance; also an archaic word for obstruction, as in without let or hindrance

indicators.note: not all means the last letter of the stop word is cut off

parts.note: halt means stop

explanation.surface: A fatal blockage that does not fully halt traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of causing death.

clue.text: Clothing and equipment from companion in ANZAC holding line

indicators.note: holding means the companion word grips the line letter inside itself

parts.note: cobber is Australian and New Zealand slang for a mate

explanation.surface: Kit issued by an Australian soldier's mate, a line of gear.
explanation.walkthrough: ANZAC (Australian and New Zealand Army Corps) points to Antipodean slang; L goes inside COBBER after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for one's gear or belongings, especially clothes.

clue.text: Vehicle returning TA unit employed among rocks

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: returning means the letters TA are read backwards

explanation.surface: A vehicle bringing back reservists from a unit stationed in rocky ground.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army; 'rocks' means gemstones, not crags.
explanation.definitionFit: The measure of weight used for gemstones, slang rocks.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory — gets a wound somewhere in theatre

parts.note: off means substandard, as in an off day

indicators.note: wound, as in twisted round, says the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A poor show: a soldier receives an injury in a theatre of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' rearranges GETSA into STAGE; 'theatre' suggests a war zone, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind the scenes, out of the audience's view.

clue.text: Be in hostile uprising? He made a lot of notes

definitions.text: He made a lot of notes

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the letters upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: taken as written
ill means unfriendly, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A call to join an enemy revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns ILL and IN together, giving LLINI. Vincenzo Bellini was an Italian opera composer.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian composer, whose operas contain many musical notes.

clue.text: Taliban's core leaving heroin after processing flower

indicators.note: processing suggests drugs being treated, so the remaining letters are reworked
leaving means the central letter departs from heroin
core asks for the middle letter of Taliban

explanation.surface: Insurgents' drug is processed and shipped down a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The core of Taliban is I; HEROIN without it is HERON, rearranged by 'processing'. 'flower' is something that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, so it is a crossword flower; this one runs through France.

clue.text: During recce, beg one to provide cover with jets

definitions.text: one to provide cover with jets

indicators.note: during means the begging word goes into the middle of the survey word

parts.note: recce is a reconnaissance, a scan of the area
pray means beg or implore

explanation.surface: A reconnaissance pilot is asked for air support from fighter jets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jets' suggests aircraft; they are jets of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol that coats a surface with fine jets of paint.

clue.text: US soldier allowed padded jacket

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
let means permitted or allowed

explanation.surface: An American serviceman is permitted to wear a quilted top.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless padded or quilted waistcoat-style garment.

clue.text: What Secretary of State was appointed to foil troop manoeuvres?

definitions.text: What Secretary of State was appointed to

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests troops being shifted around, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A minister is given a post in order to thwart army movements.
explanation.walkthrough: A Secretary of State is appointed to a ministerial department, called a portfolio.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's area of responsibility is called their brief or department in British politics.

clue.text: Name a good worker forging battleaxe

parts.note: to term something is to name it
a worker is a worker ant in crossword convention

explanation.surface: Naming a skilled labourer who makes a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battleaxe' looks like a weapon to be forged, but it means a fierce woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a domineering, overbearing woman.

clue.text: Wind of Territorials' first victory by English

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the Territorials

parts.note: a victory is a win

explanation.surface: The breeze behind the reservists' opening triumph over the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' here is the verb (to wind, twist), not the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine string is to twist or coil it around something.

clue.text: Military reversed round vehicle

indicators.note: reversed tells us to read the military abbreviation backwards

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An army convoy turns round a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for limousine, a large luxury car.

clue.text: Officer commanding one aging irregular to be travelling overseas

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding

indicators.note: irregular says the letters of one and aging are put in no set order

explanation.surface: An elderly unorthodox commander is about to go abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' rearranges ONEAGING to EANGOING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships built to cross the sea are described this way.

clue.text: A second young man takes heart for granted describing courage with carriage

parts.note: a son is a young man

indicators.note: heart for asks for the central letters of the word granted

explanation.surface: A youth's bravery is taken for granted while he rides in a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Courage and carriage share vowel sounds but not consonants, which is what the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that rhyme on vowel sounds only are assonant, as courage and carriage are.

clue.text: Plant modified drone with external money

indicators.note: with external means the money comes outside, in front of the rest

parts.note: gold is money

indicators.note: modified means the letters of drone are changed round

explanation.surface: A drone fitted with costly outer parts is planted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges DRONE into ENROD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall yellow-flowered wild plant.

clue.text: Show correspondence, including one in cypher

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed inside the cypher word

parts.note: a code is a cypher
INC is the abbreviation for including
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Writing letters that contain a secret coded message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' looks like a container signal but gives its abbreviation INC.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree or correspond with something, or to happen together.

clue.text: One found among the reeds, soldiers' leader shortly is carried by night-time flyer

indicators.note: carried by means these pieces sit inside the creature of the night

parts.note: a bat flies at night

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of soldiers

parts.note: shortly means soon
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lurking in a reed bed, with an army chief borne along by a bat.
explanation.walkthrough: The reeds are the reed section of an orchestra, not a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of a double-reed woodwind instrument sits in the reed section.

clue.text: Strictly disciplined rebukes over army vehicle in short supply

indicators.note: over means the rebukes word is turned backwards

parts.note: raps are sharp rebukes

indicators.note: in short supply means the army vehicle is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a tank is an armoured army vehicle

explanation.surface: A tough regime reprimands the army for its lack of vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and rigorously disciplined, like the ancient Greeks of Sparta.

clue.text: Old comrade is a gem

parts.note: a pal is a friend or comrade

explanation.surface: An old friend is a treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: An iridescent precious stone.

clue.text: One who has a brush with suffering, the centrepiece of investiture with Queen

parts.note: pain is suffering

indicators.note: the centrepiece of asks for the middle letter of investiture

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone who suffers a near miss in the middle of a royal ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a brush with' suggests a close encounter; it is an artist's brush.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist or decorator works with a brush.

clue.text: Travesty when American pistol must be imported to yield good results

indicators.note: must be imported to means the pistol goes inside the paying word

parts.note: to pay is to bring rewards, as in crime does not pay
rod is US slang for a handgun

explanation.surface: A grotesque situation when US guns are brought in to get results.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque imitation or mockery of something.

clue.text: Tons managed to keep current and become physically fit

indicators.note: to keep means the letters for tons and managed hold the current symbol

parts.note: to run something is to manage it, so ran
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Lifting heavy weights to stay up to date and get in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise in order to get into condition.

clue.text: Matter for an argument with chief in charge

parts.note: top means chief or leading

explanation.surface: A row with the boss who is running things.
explanation.definitionFit: The subject under discussion in a debate.

clue.text: Vocally smooth cabinet left flailing without answer

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the answer letter stands beyond the mixed-up group
flailing suggests thrashing about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A government flounders, unable to respond, while its spokesperson remains silky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flailing' rearranges CABINETL into CANTABIL; 'without' in its old sense of outside puts A after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning in a smooth, singing style.

clue.text: A serious offence abandoning final area of former war zone

indicators.note: abandoning final means the last letter goes from the war zone

parts.note: the Crimea was the scene of the Crimean War of the 1850s

explanation.surface: A grave misdeed: deserting the last part of an old battleground.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlawful act punishable by law.

clue.text: Perhaps senator is opportunely right in introducing agents

parts.note: pat means at just the right moment

indicators.note: introducing means the agents are brought into the word in

parts.note: taken as written
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A senator neatly brings in spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks senator as one example of an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman senator was a member of the noble class, an example of an aristocrat.

clue.text: Men around utility vehicle form part of target

indicators.note: around means the men letters surround the vehicle

parts.note: OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers
a ute is an Australian utility vehicle or pickup

explanation.surface: Soldiers surrounding a pickup form part of the shooting range.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring nearest the edge of an archery or shooting board.

clue.text: Surrender as soon as captured by regulars in cadre

indicators.note: captured by means a phrase is held inside the picked letters
regulars in asks for every other letter of cadre

parts.note: once means as soon as, as in once he arrives

explanation.surface: Yielding the moment soldiers in a unit are taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulars in' takes C, D, E from cadre, with ONCE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield or admit defeat.

clue.text: Cross lengthy bridge without cover

indicators.note: without cover strips the outer letters away, leaving a run from inside the words

explanation.surface: A long bridge with no roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross between two breeds or species is a mix of both.
